items.title: Is Ares' ¥612 Billion Japan Logistics Fund Altering The Investment Case For Ares Management (ARES)?
items.summary: Ares Management Corporation recently closed its Japan Logistics Development Partners V LP at its hard cap, raising ¥612 billion (about US$4 billion) for developing modern logistics facilities across key Japanese metropolitan areas, with Canada Pension Plan Investment Board committing ¥150 billion (about US$968 million) as a cornerstone investor. This fund, nearly 50% larger than its 2021 predecessor and already committed to projects representing about ¥450 billion in total investment,...

items.title: Private Equity Wants Your Broken Garage Door. Why KKR Thinks They Are Worth $2 Billion
items.summary: KKR manages nearly $800 billion in assets, yet its next big bet is a Phoenix company that fixes broken garage doors. The logic behind a $2 billion valuation reveals something unsettling about where private equity is hunting for returns.

items.title: Investors Still Want Out of Private Credit Funds Like Blackstone’s and Cliffwater’s
items.summary: Blackstone and Cliffwater have seen redemption requests of about 10% and 16%, respectively, at their private credit funds.

items.title: Ares Management (ARES) Finds Opportunity in Student Housing as Demand Remains Resilient
items.summary: Ares Management Corporation (NYSE:ARES) and The Scion Group have acquired four U.S. student housing communities for approximately $435 million, adding 2,316 beds near the University of Georgia, University of Tennessee, and Texas State University. items.title: Is Ares Management on Track to Hit Its $750B AUM Target by 2028?
items.summary: ARES is progressing well to reach its $750 billion 2028 AUM target, backed by strong fundraising and rising fee-paying assets.

items.title: Ares and Scion Buy $435M Student Housing Portfolio
items.summary: Ares and Scion bought a $435M student housing portfolio with 2,316 beds near three universities, extending a partnership formed in May.

items.title: Private Credit Stocks Are Rebounding, but Shared Loans Bring Growing Risk
items.summary: The overlapping portion of Business Development Company funds has risen from about 10% of the average portfolio in 2010 to over 55% today.
